radial_percentage.formula_status: VERIFIED (T2) as internally consistent and widely reproduced; not itself a target value
radial_percentage.theoretical_100_percent: 5H/8 of thread height (H = 0.8660*P metric per ISO 68-1 basis; H = 0.6495/TPI inch per engagement-calculator sources), physically unachievable due to crest/root truncation
radial_percentage.target_75_percent_finding: NOT VERIFIED as a standard or requirement. No Tier 1 source (ASME B94.9 table content) was obtainable -- ANSI preview returned HTTP 403. Commonly cited (70-77%) across Tier 3 sources with inconsistent stated justifications between sources.
radial_percentage.false_positive_avoided: A '75 percent' figure found in NASA-STD-5020A (p.62 of the PDF) refers to bolt preload as a percentage of ultimate tensile strength -- an unrelated concept to thread-engagement percentage. Explicitly checked and excluded from corroborating the tap-drill 75% convention.

axial_length.primary_source_obtained: NASA-STD-5020A, full text (114 pages), fetched directly from nasa.gov and read via direct PDF text extraction (not a secondary characterization)
axial_length.key_finding: NASA-STD-5020A section 4.7.4 [TFSR 23] specifies a strength-based principle for engagement length ('minimum number of engaged complete threads such that the fastener would fail in tension before threads would strip'), not a fixed percentage or fixed diameter-multiplier.
axial_length.shear_equations_found: Eq. 12-13: allowable ultimate shear load = Fsu x Am (threads in shear plane) -- confirms strength-based design approach
axial_length.blind_hole_confirmation: Section 4.7.5 [TFSR 25] confirms directly: 'Where blind holes are tapped, incomplete internal threads are present at the bottom of the hole.' -- direct primary-source support for why bottoming taps exist as a category.
axial_length.three_thread_rule_status: Cited by secondary sources as appearing in NASA-STD-5020/MIL-STD-1312-9/BAC5009, but the exact phrase was not found verbatim on the pages read in this phase -- recorded as externally-corroborated, not internally-confirmed.

what_boltlab_can_safely_calculate: Radial engagement % for a given drill diameter (pure geometry, safe)
Theoretical maximum / truncated ceiling (geometric fact, safe)
NOT a recommended target percentage (no Tier 1 source, unsafe to assert as verified)
NOT a minimum axial engagement length (formula known, but BoltLab lacks shear-strength material data to apply it)

tap_type_application_notes.schema_change: Added optional application_notes array field (entity.schema.json), each entry classified general_taxonomy / manufacturing_characteristic / typical_application / manufacturer_specific_recommendation with source, source_tier, status
tap_type_application_notes.verified_fact: bottoming_tap: 'incomplete internal threads are inherently present at the bottom of a tapped blind hole' -- sourced directly to NASA-STD-5020A section 4.7.5, a Tier 1 primary source.
